The benchmark smoke checks separate construction, valid, invalid, traversal and formatting rows; complete metrics and exact toolchain/platform metadata; and zero allocation in valid rows. BenchmarkValidation prepares the input and rule before b.Loop and reports errors in a separate row. The native gate records ten runs per category.

The test inspects the previous-elements equality scan and absence of per-call maps/input writes, requires benchmark rows at sizes 8, 64 and 1024 with zero B/op and allocs/op, and checks the documented n(n−1)/2 bound. Behaviour tests also assert unchanged inputs; documentation states no absolute latency SLA.

The source gate parses every library runtime Go file, rejects sync.Pool, package mutable state, mutable captured rule state, per-call maps and reporting callbacks or iterators in the validation ABI. Mutation fixtures prove detection. The six membership constructors build their captured maps before returning rules and only read them during validation; native probes test first and steady-state success costs.

The policy tests require all three exact Go 1.27 native pairs, current source and implementation identities, correctness and allocation gate records, exact toolchain/platform metadata, and rejection of cross-compiled evidence. Actual native results are required by the release aggregator.

The test runs all four bounded fuzz targets and requires passing seed entries. Their oracles derive expected paths, numeric bounds, slice occurrences and sorted map diagnostics independently, check input preservation and both map insertion orders. The native Linux gate runs each target for 60 seconds, and CI retains failure corpus files.

The test compiles Rule as func(T) error, checks typed struct/field/collection composition and ordered all-error paths, audits runtime exports for removed v1 engines and operators, and requires migration guidance for presence, paths, named types and concrete nil adaptation. The runtime source and allocation gates exclude context, reflection and successful-path allocation regressions.

The test requires specification and binding checkers to accept every case, verifies synthetic missing cases/gates/platforms block local or matrix completion, and compiles README and migration examples. The release aggregator itself requires every mapped case and the exact native correctness, source, race, fuzz, allocation and benchmark records for the same clean revision; a spec-only report cannot pass.
